text:
Marathon Petroleum dropped 5.5% today after escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East—specifically Iran's attacks on U.S. military installations in Kuwait and threats against shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. While crude oil prices held relatively steady (around $90/barrel), the security risks to one of the world's most critical energy chokepoints have spooked energy markets; refiners like Marathon depend on reliable oil supply flows, and disruptions to the Strait threaten both input costs and regional stability.

The sell-off also reflects a broader two-week slide (down nearly 5% since mid-November) as geopolitical risk has mounted. Even with U.S. refineries running at a healthy 95.7% capacity and adequate fuel storage, uncertainty about Middle East supply chains weighs on refiner stocks—the market is pricing in potential disruption costs rather than waiting to see if one actually materializes.
